articleTitle: Selection of Charging Station Technology to Support the Adoption of Electric Vehicles in Indonesia with the AHP-TOPSIS Method
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The transportation sector is the largest oil energy-consuming sector and the second-largest emitter of gas emissions in Indonesia. To overcome this, the Government of Indonesia issued a presidential decree for electric cars in Indonesia, which targets to accelerate the adoption of electric vehicles in Indonesia. Several obstacles will be faced in adopting an electric vehicle in Indonesia, one of which is the readiness of an electric vehicle charging station. With a high investment value and a variety of charging technology forces the government to be able to choose the right technology. The objective of this research is to select the best alternative to provide recommendations for the Indonesian government in choosing the right type of charging station technology for Indonesia. In order to accomplish the aim, a hierarchy-based model has been developed by considering nine criteria and three alternatives, namely battery swapping, inductive, and conductive. This research uses the combined method of analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS). Analysis reveals that the alternative, `Conductive Charging,' holds the first rank among all considered alternatives.

articleTitle: Use of Data Analytics in Microgrids: A Survey of Techniques
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Enabling electrical energy for geographically remote areas using renewable energy replacing the use of diesel fuel eliminating CO2 emissions is a key research focus, that the world is interested in. In recent years, the penetration of renewable resources in distribution networks has increased that it has led to a deployment of Distributed Generation (DG) at this level. The concept of microgrids popularized as it gave a solution in controlling the DGs by ensuring the network stability. A Microgrid is a small-scale distribution grid with DGs which provides electricity even during a grid failure by energy storages and load dispatch techniques. Even though they can be reliable, they pose significant challenges in maintaining the network stability and meeting economical demand. With the increase of metering devices at microgrids and the improvement of data analysis has paved the way for mitigating some of these challenges in microgrids. This paper presents a survey on data analytics techniques used in microgrids for improving the reliability and efficiency of power supply to the consumers and future trends.

articleTitle: Design of 2-Leg Inverter for Controlling of A Single Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This project aims to create an inverter to control speed of a single phase induction motor whose rpm (round per minute) can be adjusted from low rpm to power capacity through pulse width modulation. The power circuit of the 2-leg inverter was installed with 8 IGBT (insulated gate bipolar transistors) as switch and microcontroller number PIC30F4011 as circuit controlling unit. According to the test with the developed inverter for controlling a single phase induction motor, the rpm could be adjusted from zero to the power capacity. Moreover, the motor could be driven to the power capacity as specified in the plate.

articleTitle: A Novel Symmetric Battery Equalizer Topology Based on Bidirectional DC/DC Converter for Series-Connected Lithium-ion Cells
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The inhomogeneity among individual cells after several charge/discharge cycles leads to premature deterioration of series-connected Lithium-ion battery string. Therefore, cell balancing has been served as an indispensable role on the battery life preservation and the usable capacity optimization of the battery stack. This paper introduces the low-component-count and high-speed DC/DC converter based non-dissipative balancing scheme, which realizes energy interchange among the cells by charging and discharging of the inductors through switches. The justified comparison with the conventional topology demonstrates that the proposed battery equalizer performed a higher-level balancing speed because the energy transfer is not only cell by cell, but also from a cell to the multiple cells.

articleTitle: Comparison of Fuzzy Controller and PI Controller for a High Step-Up SingleSwitch Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper presents the performance comparison of fuzzy controller and PI controller for a high step-up single-switch boost converter. The high step-up single-switch boost converter is described. This converter can step the low input voltage up to the high output voltage level of 400V by using only one power switch. The high step-up voltage conversion gain, approximately 20 times, can be achieved. The control strategies for the high step-up single-switch boost converter based on the PI controller and the fuzzy controller are designed. Simulation results show the comparison of converter performance between PI controller and fuzzy controller under various operating conditions. The better performance of the converter can be obtained by using fuzzy controller compared to PI controller in the same simulation situations.

articleTitle: Office Appliance Data Classification Based on Non-intrusive Load Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: As building digitalization is accelerating, one of the challenges is making intelligent use of building energy consumption data. Since appliance-level energy consumption data is not generally available, Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring (NILM) provides novel ways to disaggregate total energy consumption into appliance-level data while ensuring the privacy of customers. This work focuses on a NILM algorithm that is applicable to common appliances and widespread smart metering infrastructure. The energy consumption data of an office was collected with a 1-min resolution and used for analysis. A fuzzy c-means clustering NILM algorithm and inter-cluster entropy were used to classify data and verify different categories of office appliances. The algorithm was proven to be able to disaggregate and classify office appliance energy consumption data with a satisfactory accuracy.

articleTitle: Terminal Sliding Mode Control (TSMC) Scheme for Current Control of Five-Phase Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In recent times, multi-phase induction motor drives have attracted attention where high overall device performance and a decrease in total power per phase are desired. The extra phases in conjunction with normal 3-phase drive ensure that the mechanism continues to function without torque ripple, disturbance and vibration even under unstable circumstances. To overcome this problem, a suitable terminal sliding mode control system may achieve a ripple-less high torque in a five-phase induction motor. The current control loop offers significant benefits to enhance the stability of the drive system. With outstanding transient responses, this device can conduct strong dynamic current management. The Terminal Sliding Mode Control based on MPCC is used to optimize the motor control system. Whereas, HOSM is introduced to eliminate the chattering phenomenon.

articleTitle: Analysis on Withstand Voltage of DC bias Device at 500kV Transformer Neutral Point
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In order to study the resistance selection of DC bias device at transformer neutral point, in this paper, a 500kV power plant model including several transformer is established based on EMTP software, The simulation results show that when the resistance of DC bias device changes in the range of 2 Ω to 10 Ω, the change of fault current passing through the neutral point of transformer is small, at the same time, the withstand voltage of DC bias device increases proportionally with the increase of resistance, the number of transformers has little effect on the current flowing through the DC bias device. Therefore, the withstand voltage of DC bias device is mainly determined by the amplitude of asymmetrical short-circuit zero sequence current. According to the research results, the design of transformer DC bias device needs to consider the resistance and withstand voltage comprehensively. When the fault zero sequence current is large, the smaller resistance should be selected as far as possible to ensure the operation of the transformer safely. The paper suggested that the power frequency withstand voltage of DC bias device of 500kV transformer should not be lower than 72kV.

articleTitle: Implementation of Vector Oriented Control of DFIG based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Control strategy is indispensable in the use of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG). Vector oriented control (VOC) is a control strategy that has been tested by many scholars in DFIG on software. Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), with the powerful capability of parallel computing and satisfying clocking frequency up to 200MHz, has widely applications in the high-speed data processing. Moreover, System Generator, as a tool developed by Xilinx, is a Simulink-based toolkit for FPGA developers. Thus, this paper implements VOC on FPGA by using System Generator. The simulation result shows that FPGA works well on VOC under the clocking frequency of 100MHz. This research solves the timing problem of loop design in System Generator and lays the foundation of real-time simulation of DFIG.

articleTitle: Second-Order Sliding-Mode Observer for Solar-Array Current Estimation
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This article focuses on the second-order sliding-mode observer which online estimates solar-array current at distinct diversified values of its one gain. The above observer is incorporated into the control system of single-phase grid-connected PV inverter and it supplants the PV current sensor. The solar-array voltage, the grid current, and the status of four switches configured in H-bridge are transmitted to the state observer. Besides, the unique constituent based on super-twisting algorithm is integrated into the observer so that the solar-array current with high ripple is estimated certainly under a momentarily brief sampling-period. Ultimately, the performance enhancement of the current estimations will be studied when the one crucial gain of the observer varies.

articleTitle: Verification on Valve Losses of LCC HVDC Converter Station in Korea
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper deals with verification of valve losses on High Voltage Direct Current(HVDC) converter stations in Korea. Technique of calculating losses is one of important verification process to evaluate systems performance, so customers have right to get accurate information of losses in project bidding process. However, it is not easy for utility company to verify maker's documents because getting information is limited from makers.Losses of a converter station can be easily estimated from calculation of two main equipments, valve and transformer, because proportion of two equipments accounts for more than 80% of the total values in the HVDC converter station. In this paper, the authors firstly analyzed calculating process of valve losses and verified if the calculated results are accorded with the reports provided from maker in accordance with the IEC standards, IEEE standard, EPRI Handbook in Jeju No.2 converter station in Korea. After that, it was verified whether the results were satisfactory compared to KEPCO's specification.

articleTitle: Impact of Cu Doping on PV Cell Parameters of NiO:Cu Nanostructure-Based Organic-Inorganic Perovskite Solar Cells
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Solar energy is abundant, reliable, and clean among all the existing renewable energy sources. Due to the fast growth of the conversion efficiency of organic-inorganic perovskite (PVT) solar cells (PSCs) has fascinated the consideration of the researchers and photovoltaic (PV) industries. To achieve high performance and stability, the selection of a hole-transport material (HTM) of PSC is essential. In this regard, we have studied the potential of solution-processed Cu-doped NiO (NiO:Cu) nanoparticles (NPs) as efficient HTL for PSCs. NiO:Cu is also able to decrease the recombination at the HTL/PVT interface. The optical loss and charge transportation rate is analyzed with the Cu doping concentration. The UV-Vis result shows that the maximum transmittance NiO:Cu HTL is obtained at a Cu doping concentration of 5%. Moreover, the time-resolved photoluminescence reviled that the same NiO:Cu HTL with Cu doping of 5% has the greatest hole transportation rate. The obtained values J<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sc</sub>, V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">oc</sub>, FF and η of the champion PSC are 21.26 mA/cm2, 1.033 V, 0.7261, and 15.95%, respectively for R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Cu/Ni</sub> = 5%.

articleTitle: Thermal Management of a High Performance Electric Motorcycle: Active vs Passive Cooling
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: High performance electric motorcycles present a complex thermal management challenge due to their high operational C-rates and compact packaging requirements with regards to volume and mass. Here passive (coolant to air) and active (refrigeration cycle) cooling mechanisms are modelled and compared for high performance use cases at ambient temperatures of 20°C, 30°C and 40°C. The performance of the vehicle is assessed on the time taken to reach the battery's temperature limit, and the power sustained at that limit. The simulation results show that reducing the size of the battery to accommodate an active cooling system leads to increased temperatures under high loads despite the increased cooling power, but allows the battery to sustain higher discharge currents when the battery temperature is limited to 70°C.

articleTitle: A Hybrid-Type High Step-Down DC/DC Converter Using a Step-Down Cross-Connected Fibonacci Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: For 48V data center applications, we present a new hybrid-type high step-down dc/dc converter with single inductor. Unlike conventional high step-down switched capacitor converters, the proposed converter is designed by connecting a step-down cross-connected Fibonacci converter to a traditional buck converter in series, where the cross-connected Fibonacci converter which is designed by switched capacitor techniques achieves high step-down gain without cascade connection of switched capacitor converter cells. Furthermore, series-connected topology with single-inductor enables high voltage gain, small size, and light weight. The given theoretical analysis and the performed simulations demonstrated that the power efficiency of the proposed high step-down converter is higher than that of the conventional high step-down converters. Concretely, the proposed converter can achieve 91%@2W and 76%@2W in the case of 1/19× and 1/53× voltage gains, respectively. Furthermore, the done breadboard experiments validated the feasibility of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of an Offshore Wind Farm on the Egyptian Coast
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In this paper, a preliminary design is applied to specify the minimum spacing between turbines to be located offshore. These spacing are affecting the wakes' interactions, which have effects on power generation and the farm occupying surface area. A numerical analysis is carried out on an offshore wind farm in the Egyptian Mediterranean Coast, to specify the optimal separation distance between the turbines. Results revealed that, the separation distance of 7 rotor diameters that is parallel to the wind direction was optimum. The separation distance of 3 rotor diameters was the optimum spacing between turbines perpendicular to the wind direction.

articleTitle: Design of an Inductor-less Step-Down AC/AC Converter Combined with a Symmetrical-Type Converter and Ladder-Type Converters
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In this paper, a new inductor-less step-down ac/ac converter is designed by using switched-capacitor (SC) techniques. Unlike existing inductor-less ac/ac converters, the proposed ac/ac converter consists of ladder-type converters nested in a symmetrical-type converter. In the proposed ac/ac converter, the 1/4× voltage gain is achieved by converting an ac input twice by the symmetrical-type converter and the ladder-type converters. The proposed new topology enables to reach not only high power efficiency but also high input power factor. To evaluate the characteristics of the proposed ac/ac inverter realizing the 1/4× voltage gain, we conducted theoretical analysis and simulation program with integrated circuit emphasis (SPICE) simulations. The SPICE simulation results demonstrated that the proposed ac/ac converter can achieve about 84% power efficiency and 0.88 input power factor when the output power is 200W.

articleTitle: Techno Selection Approach of Working Fluid for Enhancing the OTEC System Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Conversion of Ocean Thermal Energy (OTEC) is an electrical generation process that uses minor temperature variations among hot shore water and cool deep sea water. The main goal of the study is to determine the most suitable operating fluid to provide a high performance of the OTEC process. Three groups of organic fluids: wet, dry, and IOS entropic fluids, as working fluids, are investigated in this study in converting the low-grade energy of the OTEC system. A mathematical model is constructed for this purpose using the temperature gradient for the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt as a case study. The results indicate that the refrigerant R134a has a significant effect on the OTEC system efficiency with an efficiency of 2% at a constant pressure and 2.73% at a constant temperature, and on the price and the environmental issues, which all make it the optimum cooling fluid for the OTEC cycle.

articleTitle: Three-Stage Window Comparator Circuit with MOSFET-Resistor Voltage Reference
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: A window circuit is a circuit that is used to detect signals in the domain of time for detecting the amplitude of voltage or current signal and comparing it with a specified signal level. If the input signal is at the specified level, the logic signal will be output at "1". However, the logic output is "0" if the input signal is outside the window boundary. The input signal detection may be able to do more than 1 channel to achieve multi-level detection. Each channel has its own output, with the circuit being a multi-stage window comparator. There are many types of multi-stage window comparator circuits such as those used as analog window circuits in a hysteresis and determine the channel by calculating the resistance or those using an integrated circuit with input resistance as a voltage divider circuit to determine the operating range. This paper presents a three-stage window comparator circuit with MOSFET and resistor reference voltage method comparing the threshold voltage within the CMOS ICs to determine the window boundary. The window boundary has a constant according to the supply voltage, though less devices use the formats described above. The circuit can be used to detect signals in the range of 0-7 volts, divided into three levels. Testing the operation of the circuit was carried out with a computer simulation program and experimental circuits.

articleTitle: The Flow Evolution of the Atomic Layer Deposition Process: A Numerical Study of the Implimentation of a Porous Plate
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Nano-fabrication techniques are an ever-growing field that has led to the leading cutting edge nano-technologies of today. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) has manifested itself as a key player to produce highly uniform and conformal nano thin film products. However, to obtain components with enhanced properties, research is tasked to focus on the in-depth understanding of the transport phenomena of the ALD process. To accomplish this, computational techniques are adopted to efficiently analyse the ALD process. This study models the flow evolution and mass transport within an ALD reactor with and without a perforated plate to fabricate $A1_{2}O_{3}$. Within the study a perforated plate inside the shower head temporal ALD reactor is modelled as a porous medium. The numerical model of the perforated plate inside an ALD reactor is simplified by defining a region in space as a porous zone instead of directly modelling the complex perforated plate geometry inside the ALD reactor. The numerical model is then solved using ANSYS Fluent. The integration of the porous medium into the numerical modelling of the ALD process ultimately decreases the number of elements required to accurately model the ALD process, and therefore, decreases the computational resources required to analyse the process. It is found that the porous medium promotes uniform flow of gas, thus preventing circulating flow within the reactor. The perforated plate increases the uniformity of precursor distribution with O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> having a greater increase in uniformity than TMA. This is due to the difference in density. The perforated plate has a more notable impact on the flow field than on the precursor distribution.

articleTitle: Influence of Single and Double-Atom Metal Doping on the Electrocatalytic Hydrogen Evolution Activity of 2D-MoS2 Surface
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The Hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) is an important process during electrocatalytic water splitting for hydrogen energy generation. Two dimensional MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> has been considered as a promising alternative to Pt-based catalysts in the hydrogen evolution reaction. However, the highest contribution for the catalytic activity of 2D-MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is from its edge sites, this in turn leaves many in-plane domains useless. In this study, the effect of single and double atom metal (Pt, Ni and Pt-Ni) doping on HER catalytic activity of in-plane atoms was investigated using density functional theory calculations. The Gibbs free energy of adsorbed hydrogen on pristine MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> decreased from 1.86eV to -0.08eV in PtNi co-doped MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This demonstrates enhanced catalytic activity of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> due to atomic doping. The enhanced catalytic activity may also be attributed to the observed changes in structural and electronic properties.

articleTitle: Synthesis and Analysis of a Dual-Input Cross-Connected Charge Pump with Gain Selecting Functions
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: For small power applications, we propose a dualinput cross-connected charge pump with gain selecting functions. The proposed dc/dc converter has the significant features, namely, hybrid input sources, gain selecting function, and cross-connected structure. In the proposed dc/dc converter, a dc output is provided to an output load by combing a battery input with a scavenged energy input. By alleviating energy consumption of the battery source, the proposed dc/dc converter offers a long lifetime of batteries. Furthermore, the gain selecting function can adjust the voltage gain of the proposed dc/dc converter according to the voltage level of the scavenged energy source. Therefore, the proposed dc/dc converter can achieve a wide input range. Additionally, the cross-connected structure provides high voltage gain and small ripple in the proposed dc/dc converter. The characteristics of the proposed dc/dc converter were clarified by theoretical analysis using a six-terminal equivalent mode. Furthermore, by comparing the proposed dc/dc converter with series-parallel dc/dc converter, traditional charge pump, and Fibonacci dc/dc converter, the effectiveness of the proposed dc/dc converter was confirmed by simulation program with integrated circuit emphasis (SPICE) simulations. In addition, we validated the feasibility of the proposed topology through breadboard experiments.

articleTitle: An Analysis Method for Design of a Cross-connected Fibonacci Switched Capacitor Converter
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: A switched capacitor converter (SCC) is designed without magnetic components, the characteristic of which can reduce circuit sizes and fit in portable devices. Among many types of SCCs, a cross-connected Fibonacci SCC (CCFSCC) was suggested but was analyzed, neglecting some circuit parameters such as its operation frequency and capacitance in previous studies. This study proposes an analysis method to optimize the CCFSCC, and to provide its hardware design guidance. From the proposed method, the operation frequency and capacitances of capacitors of the CCFSCC can be selected. To confirm the reliability of the suggested method, we compare the modeled and simulated results. The absolute difference between two outcomes is under 0.1 on average.

articleTitle: Improvement of Atomic Layer Deposition Quality Control Method
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Atomic layer deposition (ALD) can be used in the fabrication of new materials, optimization of battery electrode surfaces and many other fields. Data-driven quality control method of ALD was studied in this paper, including quality inspection based on image segmentation and quality prediction based on decision tree. The results showed that the algorithms designed in this paper were effective and provided new solutions for the improvement of ALD.

articleTitle: Improvement Energy Conservation of Small Medium Economic in Thailand Using Energy Matrix Management Case Study: Agriculture Knife Industry
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The improvement energy conservation system has been challenging and interesting for small and medium enterprises (SME) of Thailand. This paper presents energy conservation in the knife industry used energy management and brainstorming workshop. Methodology applied energy matrix management and collaboration with community. The results show that this research can be reduce the energy consumption and enhancement of machinery. Moreover, the participant community induced to sustainable development.

articleTitle: A Charge-Transferring Zero-Current-Switching DC-DC Current-Output Converter for Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper proposes and implements a DC current driving technology for induction motors based on the principle of magnetomotive force combination. The scheme of induction motors driven by DC current source maintains the key merits of their counterparts using current source inverters, and also overcome shortcomings of current source inverters, such as bulky scale and high cost. Its working principles of DC current driving technology are explained in details. To generate the DC current for induction motor driving, a charge-transferring zero-current switching (CT-ZCS) DC current-output converter and its operating principle are proposed and elucidated, which can be classified as a kind of quasi-resonant converters. Moreover, mathematical model of the CT-ZCS DC current conversion circuit is developed by using symbolic analysis and discrete mapping modeling. Besides, a prototype was built for experimental test. Both simulation and experimental results are given to verify the feasibility of the proposed CT-ZCS DCDC current-output converter for induction motor.

articleTitle: Proposal to optimize Electricity Consumption Costs for Regulated Clients in Medium and Low Voltage - Case Study: Peru
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This article presents the results of the savings for electricity consumption obtained from the analysis and application of the tariff options for regulated customers in medium and low voltage in the Peruvian market. The methodology considers the evaluation of 152 consumption profiles of various clients in the commercial and industrial sector, with which simulation sheets were designed for the construction of the load diagrams in order to know the production cycles of the companies. Based on the load diagram and the concepts contemplated in each electricity tariff, the billing scenarios were simulated in the different existing options in order to choose the most convenient tariff for the analyzed company, finding economic reductions up to 23% for the energy payment electrical power as shown in the present study. Finally, a summary table of the rate options associated with the different companies according to their business activity is presented, which will serve as a guide for owners and/or administrators when choosing a rate option.

articleTitle: A Switched-Capacitor Step-Down DC-DC Converter with Specialized for Conversion Ratio around 1
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper proposes an SC step-down DC-DC converter which improves the response and the power conversion efficiency, under the condition that the conversion ratio is closed to 1. The proposed circuit is based on a digital-selecting type SC converter. The SPICE simulations showed that the start-up response and the power conversion efficiency of the proposed converter are higher than those of the digital-selecting type SC converter when conversion ratio is 2/3 or more.

articleTitle: A Study on Data Requirements for Power Disaggregation
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: While much research is being done on power disaggregation analysis, there is a lack of discussion on the data requirements of the appliance under analysis. In this paper, we present four new data requirements for power disaggregation analysis and explain implementation methods to verify them. The experimental results applied to the test appliance data are also introduced. In conclusion, this paper insists that validation of the data requirements should be an essential prerequisite step prior to developing a power disaggregation analysis model.

articleTitle: Accelerated State-of-Health Estimation for Battery Recycling, using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: The recycling of lithium-ion batteries gains more and more importance due to an increased amount of electric vehicles. Not all cells in a used battery have already reached their end of life criterion and can still be employed for second life applications. However, the characterization of returned cells is often more expensive than the economic benefit of further usage. This paper proposes an accelerated state-of-health estimation by employing neural networks in the recycling process. An overall model incorporates the aging prediction and automatically decides if a cell should still be operated in first- or second-life applications or already reached the end of its life cycle. In this case, the battery cell will be recycled and the recovered electrode material can be added to the cell manufacturing process. Therefore, this process reduces the initial production costs as well as the negative environmental impact.

articleTitle: The Behavior Investigation of a Three-Phase Interleaved Boost Converter Under Open-Circuited Switch Fault Conditions
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This paper investigates the behavior of the three-phase interleaved boost converter for renewable energy system under open-circuited switch fault conditions. It is expected that the faulty switches of the converter can be correctly detected in a very short time by taking the consideration on the converter behaviors under various operation conditions. In this paper the three-phase interleaved boost converter topology is firstly described. The PI controller is then properly designed in order to obtain the satisfactory converter performance. The phase-shift technique is also employed for ripple cancellation purpose, resulting in small ripples in the inductor currents and the capacitor voltage. Finally, the simulation results show the behavior investigation of the interleaved boost converter under healthy and faulty switch operating conditions. The input current, the output voltage and three inductor currents are deeply considered in order to develop the appropriate fault detection strategy for the future work.

articleTitle: Operation Pattern and Feasibility Analysis of the Mobile Charging Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: At present, the development of electric vehicles (EVs) is limited on account of the confined popularization for the charging station, meanwhile the decreasing service rate and the operational difficulty resulted from the low proportion of EV are constraining the prospect of the charging station, which jointly makes the interaction that hinders each other's progress. In allusion to the phenomenon mentioned above, the innovative idea of using the mobile charging vehicles (MCVs) to replace the charging station is proposed. This article introduces the MCVs' operation pattern and analyzes the advantages compared with the charging station. The economic efficiency is also analyzed between two patterns of charging. The purpose of this article is to accelerate the development of charging facility and EVs.

articleTitle: Principle Analysis of anti-skid decoupling Control of Distributed Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Nonlinearity, unexpected road conditions and varying vehicle parameters make a challenge to robust adhesion control of vehicles. This paper mainly analyzes the coupling relationship between the anti-skid control of distributed electric vehicle (EV) drive and the tire - ground nonlinear characteristics and their changes. Based on the single-wheel dynamics model, the dynamic characteristics of EV power transmission are analyzed by using the small signal increment method, and the coupling characteristics of anti-skid control and road surface characteristics under different velocity intervals and adhesion state are analyzed based on the time-scale difference of electromechanical physical quantity. Analysis shows that, due to fast torque response of electric cars, the design of driving anti-skid control need not consider nonlinearity of tire-road and its change in different speeds and adhesion states of electric cars, so the design of driving anti-skid controller is simplified, which provides a theoretical basis for obtaining basically consistent driving anti-skid control performance under different road conditions. In this paper, PI controller independent of road characteristic is taken as the object to carry out the joint simulation verification based on MATLAB and CARSIM, proving the correctness of the theoretical analysis. The decoupling control conclusion can be extended to other electrical traffic equipment with non-linear load characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Power Distribution System Reliability Indices, Niamey, Niger
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: Decades of reliability indices' (RI) investigation led most utility companies to rise the standard of their respective grid. Both poor power reliability and quality have devastating effects on customers. This paper attempts to estimate the RI of the Nigerien state-owned utility company, NIGELEC. The latter served over 314,570 customers in 2017. For the purpose of this study, four administrative zones, viz., Goudel, Yantala, Right Riverbank, and Koubya were selected. They have 78,945 customers altogether. The conventional RIs are no longer fit to view the extent to which daily power outages undermine the social and economic wellbeing of the residents. A new power reliability concept, “Customer Enjoy Without Interruption Index (CEWII),” was proposed; CEWII represents the exact number of days enjoyed without outage. Results revealed that CEWII was 3 days or 9.6S% for May 2014. Results also showed a SAIFI as high as 0.37 for May. In sum, repetitive outages are persisting as Niger, on three occasions, missed its chances to reach energy independence.

articleTitle: Reduction of Production Cost for Beef Fattening Cattle by DC Solar-Cell Water Pump
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This article aimed to assess the reduction of production costs for beef-fattening cattle by using a DC solar-cell water pump. The reduction of production costs for beef-fattening cattle by DC solar-cell water pump used two 330-W solar panels and a water pump system with 0.5 HP to produce food for the cattle. The machine pumps groundwater to grass and corn fields, which are then used to feed the cattle. The duration of the experiment was 4 months. The results demonstrated that the use of solar energy could greatly reduce production costs. Based on comparison with older machines, the reduction amounted to 41%. Thus, the use of solar energy should be promoted in the agricultural sector at the regional level.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Fan-Shaped Nozzle Structure Based on CFD
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: In order to select nozzle reasonably, improve the utilization rate of pesticide and enhance the atomization effect of nozzle, the internal flow field of fan-shaped nozzle with different terminal structure under the same parameters was simulated and analyzed. By using FLUENT software, through the analysis of the velocity and pressure of the internal flow field, three fan-shaped nozzles with different terminal structures are compared. In the case that the three structural parameters of nozzle length, inner cavity diameter and groove angle are consistent, the simulation of round head type, cone type and innovative type is compared. The results show that among the three nozzle structures, the improved innovative nozzle has the best velocity uniformity in the nozzle area, and the speed and pressure changes are more stable. The comprehensive performance has obvious advantages over the other two nozzles, and has better atomization effect and pesticide utilization rate.

articleTitle: An Inductor-Less AC/DC Converter Using a Bipolar Cockcroft-Walton Multilier and a Cross-Coupled Charge Pump
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: For low-voltage vibration energy harvesting, such as 0.5V@50Hz input, this paper presents a novel inductor-less step-up ac/dc converter. In the proposed ac/dc converter, high voltage gain can be achieved by combing a cross-coupled charge pump with a bipolar Cockcroft-Walton multiplier, where a rectifier-less design is realized by the bipolar Cockcroft-Walton multiplier. Furthermore, small EMI (Electro-Magnetic Interference) is provided by the inductor-less design. The performance of the proposed ac/dc converter with 12×step-up gain is evalutaed by theoretical analysis and SPICE (Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis) simulations. The SPICE simulations demonstrated that the power efficiency of the proposed converter is about 88%@1mW with 1% ripple factor. Furthermore, breadboard experiments verify the feasibility of the proposed inductor-less topology.

articleTitle: Controller Chip Design of Serial-Parallel-Switched-Capacitor Coupled-Inductor Boost DC-AC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: This work is focused on the controller chip design/ implementation of serial-parallel-switched-capacitor coupledinductor (SPSCCI) inverter applied to high-gain boost DC-AC conversion. The controlled plant is its power part made up of SPSCCI booster and DC-link inverter to perform a practical DC-AC conversion from 12V to 110VRMS, 60Hz. Here, for achieving this goal, the controller is its control part constructed by sinusoidal pulse-width-modulation (SPWM) compensator plus phase generator, and then is implemented under Cadence full-custom design through pre-layout simulation (PRE-SIM) and post-layout simulation (POST-SIM) on a fabricated chip of integrated circuit: no. D35-105B-E0008, TSMC 0.35μm 2P4M, 1500×1500μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 5.0V, 2.68mW, max frequency 200kHz. Finally, with the help of this controller chip, a closed-loop prototype circuit of this SPSCCI can be realized and verified experimentally for some test cases of DC-AC to validate the feasibility of this inverter.

articleTitle: Cooperative Game Operation Strategy of a Hydropower-Photovoltaic-Pumped Storage System in the Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2020 3rd International Conference on Power and Energy Applications (ICPEA)
abstract: With the development of photovoltaic (PV) power and electricity markets, PV power station is increasingly integrated into the power grid for participating in the electricity markets. Each station participates in the electricity market alone can get a high profit, but actually, they can obtain an even higher profit through cooperation. Based on cooperative game theory, this study investigates a joint operation framework, which is composed of a hydropower station, a PV station and a pumped storage station, to participate in electricity market. The objective function is to improve the profit of each station and their overall profit through cooperation. The feasibility of the joint operation station is verified by comparing with their independent operation. The results show that when they cooperate with each other, the profits of a hydropower station, a PV station and a pumped storage station can increase by 2.67%, 79.77% and 106.45%, respectively. Also, no PV power is abandoned under the condition of the cooperation operation.
